library(nlmixr2lib)

```

# Model and source

Redhi 2026 explored repurposing the anticancer ATR-kinase inhibitor berzosertib
(VE-822 / VX-970 / M6620) as an antimalarial. They built a sequential
pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) model in *Plasmodium falciparum*-infected
humanized mice and then predicted an efficacious human dose by combining a human
population PK model (derived from a PK-Sim PBPK model) with the mouse-derived
unbound-plasma PD parameters. Two model files are packaged:

1. `Redhi_2026_berzosertib_mouse` -- one-compartment whole-blood PK (first-order
   absorption and linear elimination) driving a direct-effect parasitemia model
   (exponential growth minus a sigmoidal kill), fitted to NSG mice.
2. `Redhi_2026_berzosertib_human` -- two-compartment unbound-plasma PK after 1-h
   IV infusion, with allometric weight scaling, driving the same parasitemia
   model with the unbound-plasma EC50, used for the human dose prediction.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Redhi_2026_berzosertib_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70303>

```{r load-models}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Redhi_2026_berzosertib_mouse")
mod_human <- readModelDb("Redhi_2026_berzosertib_human")
```

# Population

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Redhi_2026_berzosertib_mouse")()$population)
str(readModelDb("Redhi_2026_berzosertib_human")()$population)
```

## Closed-form check: the minimum parasiticidal concentration (Eq. 3)

The MPC is the EC90, defined (Eq. 3) as `MPC = EC50 * (90 / (100 - 90))^(1/H)`.
Both models expose it as the derived variable `mpc`, and it reproduces the
Table 1 values exactly.

```{r mpc-check}
mpc_mouse <- 13.24 * 9^(1 / 7) # whole blood
mpc_human <- 0.58 * 9^(1 / 7) # unbound plasma
c(mouse = mpc_mouse, human = mpc_human)
# Table 1: whole-blood MPC = 18.12 ng/mL; unbound-plasma MPC = 0.79 ng/mL.
stopifnot(abs(mpc_mouse - 18.12) < 0.05, abs(mpc_human - 0.79) < 0.01)
```

The unbound values follow from the whole-blood values via the mouse blood-to-plasma
ratio (2.06) and fraction unbound (0.09): `13.24 * 0.09 / 2.06 = 0.578` and
`18.12 * 0.09 / 2.06 = 0.792`, matching the Table 1 unbound EC50 (0.58) and
MPC (0.79).

```{r unbound-check}
stopifnot(
  abs(13.24 * 0.09 / 2.06 - 0.58) < 0.01,
  abs(18.12 * 0.09 / 2.06 - 0.79) < 0.01
)
```

# Mouse whole-blood PK

The dose-escalation study gave 0.5-20 mg/kg once daily; the mouse weighed
25-35 g. The simulation below uses 0.03 kg. Table S3 reports the single-dose
non-compartmental Cmax and AUC0-24 at each dose level.

```{r mouse-pk-sim}
mod_mouse_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_mouse)
wt_mouse <- 0.03

doses_mgkg <- c(0.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 20)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.1))))

make_mouse_pk <- function(i) {
  d <- doses_mgkg[i]
  tag <- paste0(d, " mg/kg")
  dose <- tibble::tibble(id = i, time = 0, amt = d * wt_mouse, evid = 1, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tibble::tibble(id = i, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "parasites")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(arm = tag)
}
ev_mouse <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_mgkg), make_mouse_pk))
sim_mouse_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse_typ, events = ev_mouse, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r mouse-pknca}
conc_mouse <- sim_mouse_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
dose_mouse <- ev_mouse |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

nca_mouse <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_mouse, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_mouse, amt ~ time | arm + id, route = "extravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

published_mouse <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,        ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "0.5 mg/kg",     20,       99,
  "5 mg/kg",       61,      684,
  "7.5 mg/kg",     95,      776,
  "10 mg/kg",     123,     1213,
  "15 mg/kg",     157,     1901,
  "20 mg/kg",     311,     3019
)

cmp_mouse <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_mouse,
  reference = published_mouse,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "h*ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_mouse, caption = "Typical mouse (30 g) single-dose Cmax and AUC0-24 vs. Table S3. * differs by >20%.")
```

The model's structural PK (linear, dose-proportional) reproduces the Table S3
central dose levels closely; the lowest (0.5 mg/kg) and highest (20 mg/kg)
levels sit further off, as the Table S3 Cmax is not perfectly dose-proportional
there (the paper itself notes the 20 mg/kg exposure is disproportionately high).

```{r mouse-pknca-check}
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_mouse)
auc10 <- nca_df$PPORRES[nca_df$arm == "10 mg/kg" & nca_df$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
# Deterministic typical-value solve at the central 10 mg/kg level.
stopifnot(abs(auc10 / 1213 - 1) < 0.1)
```

# Human unbound-plasma PK and the dose prediction

The human model is parameterized on unbound plasma concentration. Table 3 of the
paper reports the unbound-plasma Cmax and AUC0-inf for the candidate antimalarial
regimens and the clinical MTD.

```{r human-sim}
mod_human_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_human)
wt_human <- 72.4

# Figure 4 shows four regimens over three parasite lifecycles (156 h): a single
# 440 mg infusion, and the 145 q48h, 75 q24h and 35 q12h courses.
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,         ~dose, ~ii, ~addl,
  "440 mg single",    440,  24,     0,
  "145 mg q48h x3",   145,  48,     2,
  "75 mg q24h x6",     75,  24,     5,
  "35 mg q12h x12",    35,  12,    11
)

obs_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 160, by = 0.25))))

make_human <- function(i, dat) {
  r <- dat[i, ]
  dose <- tibble::tibble(
    id = i, time = seq(0, by = r$ii, length.out = r$addl + 1),
    amt = r$dose, evid = 1, cmt = "central", dur = 1, WT = wt_human
  )
  obs <- tibble::tibble(id = i, time = obs_h, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "parasites",
                        dur = NA_real_, WT = wt_human)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = r$regimen)
}
ev_human <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), make_human, dat = regimens))
sim_human <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human_typ, events = ev_human, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r human-pknca}
# Table 3 reports the per-dose Cmax and the cumulative AUC0-inf of ONE course.
# Because the model is linear, the course AUC0-inf is the single-dose AUC0-inf
# times the number of doses (6 for the 440 mg twice-weekly cycle, 6 for 75 mg
# daily, 12 for 35 mg 12-hourly) -- exactly how the paper computes it (e.g. a
# single 75 mg dose integrates to about 104 ng.h/mL and 6 x 104 = 624). NCA is
# therefore run on one infusion per dose level with a long terminal grid, and
# the AUC is scaled by the dose count.
dose_levels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,               ~dose, ~ndose,
  "440 mg MTD (1 cycle)",   440,      6,
  "75 mg q24h x6",           75,      6,
  "35 mg q12h x12",          35,     12
)
obs_sd <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), seq(25, 6000, by = 5))))
make_sd <- function(i) {
  r <- dose_levels[i, ]
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(id = i, time = 0, amt = r$dose, evid = 1, cmt = "central",
                   dur = 1, WT = wt_human),
    tibble::tibble(id = i, time = obs_sd, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "parasites",
                   dur = NA_real_, WT = wt_human)
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = r$regimen)
}
ev_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(dose_levels)), make_sd))
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_human_typ, events = ev_sd, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_sd <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dplyr::filter(sim_sd, !is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen),
                   Cc ~ time | regimen + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dplyr::filter(ev_sd, evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen),
                   amt ~ time | regimen + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))

nca_hdf <- as.data.frame(nca_sd) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dose_levels, by = "regimen")
simulated_h <- nca_hdf |>
  dplyr::mutate(value = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs", PPORRES * ndose, PPORRES)) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, PPTESTCD, value) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)

published_h <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,               ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs,
  "440 mg MTD (1 cycle)",   116,        3571,
  "75 mg q24h x6",           22,         624,
  "35 mg q12h x12",          11,         567
)

cmp_h <- published_h |>
  dplyr::rename(cmax_ref = cmax, auc_ref = aucinf.obs) |>
  dplyr::left_join(simulated_h, by = "regimen") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Regimen = regimen,
    `Cmax ref (ng/mL)` = cmax_ref,
    `Cmax sim (ng/mL)` = round(cmax, 1),
    `Cmax % diff` = sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * (cmax / cmax_ref - 1)),
    `AUC0-inf ref (h*ng/mL)` = auc_ref,
    `AUC0-inf sim (h*ng/mL)` = round(aucinf.obs, 0),
    `AUC % diff` = sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * (aucinf.obs / auc_ref - 1))
  )
knitr::kable(cmp_h, caption = "Typical-subject unbound-plasma per-dose Cmax and one-course AUC0-inf (single-dose AUC x dose count) vs. Table 3.")
```

```{r human-pknca-check}
sim_vals <- function(reg, what) simulated_h[[what]][simulated_h$regimen == reg]
# 75 mg q24h x6 is the paper's proposed efficacious antimalarial regimen.
stopifnot(
  abs(sim_vals("75 mg q24h x6", "cmax") / 22 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(sim_vals("75 mg q24h x6", "aucinf.obs") / 624 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(sim_vals("440 mg MTD (1 cycle)", "aucinf.obs") / 3571 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

The proposed efficacious regimen 75 mg q24h x6 reproduces the Table 3
unbound-plasma Cmax (22 ng/mL) and AUC0-inf (624 ng.h/mL). All simulated unbound
Cmax values sit well below the whole-blood MPC-equivalent exposure of the MTD,
reproducing the paper's central finding that the antimalarial exposure is several
fold below the clinical safety margin.

# Human exposure-response (Figure 4) and a known source inconsistency

Figure 4 shows the unbound plasma concentration (Cc) and the parasitemia (P) for
each regimen over three parasite lifecycles (156 h), starting from 1%
parasitemia. The packaged model reproduces the concentration panels exactly (the
Cc values above), but the parasitemia panel exposes an internal inconsistency in
the published PD parameters.

```{r human-cc, fig.height = 4}
sim_human |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 156) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.79, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Unbound plasma Cc (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Redhi 2026 (typical subject); dashed line = unbound MPC 0.79 ng/mL."
  )
```

```{r human-pd}
sim_human |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(parasites), time <= 156) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, parasites, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.01, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Parasitemia P (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4b of Redhi 2026 (typical subject); dashed line = 0.01% limit of detection."
  )
```

With the parasite growth rate `Kgrowth = 0.038 /h` and kill rate
`Kkill = 0.058 /h` fixed from Table 1, the maximal net rate of parasite decline
(when the sigmoidal effect saturates at 1) is `0.058 - 0.038 = 0.020 /h`. Over
the 156-h treatment window this clears at most `1% * exp(-0.020 * 156) = 0.045%`,
so the typical subject does not reach the 0.01% limit of detection. The paper's
own Figure 4b, however, shows the 75 mg q24h and 35 mg q12h regimens reaching
0.01% at about 140 h, which implies a net decline of roughly
`log(100) / 140 = 0.033 /h` -- about 60% faster than the published rate
constants support.

```{r pd-inconsistency}
net_rate <- 0.058 - 0.038 # /h, from Table 1
minP_typ <- min(sim_human$parasites[sim_human$regimen == "75 mg q24h x6"], na.rm = TRUE)
c(net_rate = net_rate, predicted_floor = 1 * exp(-net_rate * 156), minP_typ = minP_typ)
# The verbatim model is internally self-consistent: the simulated nadir matches
# the analytic floor set by the net growth-kill balance. This asserts the
# packaged parameters are carried as published, and brackets the ~0.03-0.04%
# nadir that is the known deviation from the paper's figure.
stopifnot(
  abs(net_rate - 0.020) < 1e-9,
  minP_typ > 0.02, minP_typ < 0.06
)
```

This is carried as a documented source inconsistency, not a transcription error:
the PK layer (Cc, Cmax, AUC, MPC) reproduces the paper exactly, so the packaged
model is sound for exposure prediction and for the exposure-vs-MPC comparison
that drives the paper's dose selection. Only the absolute parasite-clearance
*time* is faster in the paper's figure than its tabulated rate constants permit.
Nothing was tuned to close the gap.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mouse initial parasitemia (`lrbase_parasites` = 0.6%).** The PK-PD fit
  seeded each mouse at its own observed day-3 parasitemia, which is not
  tabulated. 0.6% is the day-3 group mean read from Figure 1a (all groups lie
  between 0.50% and 0.75%). It is `fixed()` and affects only the absolute
  parasitemia trajectory, not the PK or the rate constants.
* **Mouse dosing in mg.** Doses are reported in mg/kg; the model takes mg, so a
  user multiplies the mg/kg dose by the body weight (kg) to get the amount. The
  vignette uses 0.03 kg.
* **Human allometric scaling.** Table S6 reports the unbound PK parameters per kg
  of body weight; the model restores the absolute parameter with the fixed
  exponents (0.75 on CL and Q, 1 on Vc and Vp) centred on the 72.4 kg mean of
  the 20 simulated subjects. Age and sex were tested and not retained.
* **Human PK provenance.** The human parameters were estimated from
  concentration-time profiles simulated by the authors' PK-Sim PBPK model, not
  from measured clinical PK. The PBPK model itself was optimized and verified
  against total-plasma clinical data (Table 2) and is not re-implemented here;
  the packaged model is the downstream population PK model of the unbound plasma
  (Table S6).
* **PD parameter inconsistency.** See the previous section: the published growth
  and kill rate constants imply a slower parasite clearance than the paper's
  Figure 4 shows. Carried verbatim with a numeric assertion bracketing the
  deviation.
* **No recrudescence.** The paper notes that parasite recrudescence was not
  included in the PK-PD model; the packaged model likewise has no dormant or
  recrudescent pool.
```
